name: Naver second data center Eumseong / Chungbuk Innovation City candidate site
developer: Naver; Chungcheongbuk-do and Eumseong-gun as site promoters
notes: Eumseong/Chungbuk Innovation City was one of ten shortlisted locations visited for Naver's second data center in 2019, with reports describing a KRW 540 billion project. Naver ultimately built and opened GAK Sejong, so this candidate is treated as rejected/not selected rather than an active Eumseong project.

name: Jecheon Internet Data Center, 4th Industrial Complex
developer: Welcome Asset Management consortium; Jecheon-si; Chungcheongbuk-do
notes: Jecheon and Chungcheongbuk-do signed an MOU for a data center in the planned 4th Industrial Complex on about 33,000 sq m. Local reports cite 40 MW and roughly KRW 600 billion investment.

name: Jecheon renewable-energy data center, 4th Industrial Complex
developer: Valmax Technology; Fine Asset Management; Namsa Dream Energy; Jecheon-si
notes: Jecheon signed an investment agreement for a KRW 500 billion eco-friendly renewable-energy data center in the 4th Industrial Complex. NewsPim reports a 60,600 sq m site and 20 MW scale using solar, biogas, and biomass energy.

name: NAVER Data Center GAK Sejong
notes: NAVER officially launched its second in-house data center, GAK Sejong, in Sejong on 2023-11-08. Data Center Dynamics and DataCenterMap list the Sejong campus at 270 MW; NAVER describes it as hyperscale AI/cloud infrastructure.

name: Okestro Cloud Sejong Finance Center II data center
notes: Sejong and Okestro Cloud signed a 2025 MOU for a KRW 700 billion data center in the vacant Sejong Finance Center II building, with reports citing up to 40 MW and a 2027 target. A 2026 local report says the plan was scrapped, so current status is recorded as rejected/cancelled.

name: Dobong-gu public data center / DBDBMAP data aggregation platform
notes: This is a municipal public-data/data aggregation platform rather than a commercial colocation or hyperscale facility. Included because multiple local reports describe Dobong-gu's public data center vision and DBDBMAP/data aggregation infrastructure; no MW capacity disclosed.
